_doc: People thanked in the About dialog's thanks list (map_template.contributor_credits).
A name enters only as the person gave it to be credited: the `credit` of a
an e-mail that asks for it, or the handle of a GitHub comment or pull request.
Added at triage when the report was acted on (fixed, or confirmed and queued).
Not added: a name that is offensive, impersonates someone, or carries contact
details or a link. Removed on request, no questions.
Fields: name (as given, at most 60 characters), added (ISO date), via (card | email |
github), slugs (the appellations the report concerned), report (one line: what it
led to), url (optional, set by the curator, never typed by a visitor: the https
address of the public profile the person is known by — a GitHub handle's
https://github.com/<handle>; the name links to it).

contributors.name: Tom Van Oppens
contributors.report: Champagne's boundaries: the map draws the 635-commune aire géographique while the vineyard's parcels lie in 319 communes and INAO publishes no parcel layer — the card now says so; a better drawing is queued.

contributors.name: Reinier Broeks
contributors.report: Feedback by chat and e-mail (credit confirmed to Boris): his Druivenatlas grape links showed that a filtered view could not be shared — the view now lives in the URL, with a share dialog and an embed (2026-10-22) — and that grape labels carried colour codes and line breaks («Barbera N.», «Cabernet- Sauvignon»), now a vote over the regulators' spellings (2026-10-23).

contributors.name: wayne530
contributors.report: Comment on pull request #19 (2026-09-23), the AU / US work: US AVAs set no grape rules, only the varietal labelling rule (75-85-95), and TTB's AVA polygons are the official ones and differ from UC Davis's — queued for the US geometry and roster model.
